source: Sentinel-1 radar ship detections from the yasumorishima/hormuz-ais dataset (sar/det and sar/scenes tables, detector v1): bright compact objects on the water, filtered to vessel-sized candidates. Copernicus Sentinel data is free and open; the detector output is the dataset author's.
note: A detection is a radar contact, not an identified ship. Contacts within 0.5 km of the shore (16251) were dropped as coastal clutter, and 1316 contacts at spots that light up in 6 or more scenes were dropped as fixed structures (platforms, buoys, islets). 'match' names the AIS vessel (MMSI) whose interpolated position at the scene time is within 1.5 km. Each scene carries 'ais', the number of archived AIS ships that could be positioned at that moment, 'population', the number of ships the monitor saw in the region on the fetch day, and 'coverage' (good: 80% or more of the population positioned, partial: 30% or more, thin). The archive follows strait crossers and anchored ships, not every vessel in the Gulf, so an unmatched contact only suggests a dark ship when coverage is good.
